raw:
Yewyn Corrford married Kadan Corrley at Kelmere in Chapter 16, and the couple lived in Kelmere from then on. The record shows no later move for her. Yewyn Haskick, who married Tatho Brackick and later lived in Salcombe and Wilholt, is a different person.

Answer: Kelmere

Luena's most recent move in the record is in Chapter 31, where she left Wilwick and settled in Ostcombe. Rozek followed her there. Later chapters show her son moving to Elmhaven, but nothing shows Luena moving again.

Answer: Ostcombe

Fewyn Stenworth's moves, in order:
- Chapter 7: followed someone to Gulhaven.
- Chapter 34: moved from Gulhaven to Yarlby.
- Chapter 40: "Fewyn followed him to Torton within the month."

The chapter 40 line says only "Fewyn", but Fewyn Stenworth is the only Fewyn in the record, so I take it to be her. It is the latest relevant information.

Answer: Torton

Havie married Isric Thornmere and lived in Ostcombe (Ch. 28). In Ch. 36 Havie moved to Staveford, and in Ch. 39 moved to Dunby, with Isric Thornmere also going to live in Dunby. No later move is recorded.

Answer: Dunby

Wenelle married Rovus and lived in Ostcombe. In chapter 22 she "went along to live in Kelmere as well." Later births (chapters 25 and 37) say the family lived in Kelmere. Nothing later records another move.

Answer: Kelmere

Rinelle Corrley married Kadrek Brackick and lived in Kelford. After a quarrel she moved to Torton (Ch. 9), then to Wilholt (Ch. 15), where the family was still living in Chapter 25. In Chapter 35 she "went along to live in Torton as well." Later passages show her talking and complaining of an aching back, but no further move for her. Chapter 38's move to Wilwick is Harine's, not hers.

Answer: Torton

The latest relevant information is in Chapter 38: a daughter, Kamira Stenenridge, was born to Movie Prydenridge and Thizek Stenenridge, and the family lived in Elmhaven. Movie Prydenridge went to live in Elmhaven in Chapter 33. No later passage shows Thizek moving elsewhere.

Answer: Elmhaven

Lurald Stenworth married Nerine Prydenridge in Chapter 25, and the couple lived in Ostcombe from then on. Their son Istho was born there as well. No later passage shows Lurald moving away from Ostcombe. Earlier, he had lived in Kelford and then Dunstead with Luwyn Brackick.

Answer: Ostcombe

Pelde Stenworth was born into the Torton household. She later married Davus (as Pelde Stenson) in Torton, which is a different line, but in Chapter 34 Pelde Stenworth took Sebin Brackick in marriage at Torton, and the couple lived in Torton from then on. In Chapter 37 their daughter Elvie Brackick was born, and the family lived in Torton. No later move for Pelde Stenworth is recorded. The "went along to live" entries after that point name other people (Harine, Isric Thornmere, Lura), not Pelde.

Answer: Torton

Gadrek Prydenridge married in Chapter 29 and the couple lived in Ostcombe from then on. No later paragraph mentions him moving elsewhere. The "went along to live in" entries after that refer to other people.

Answer: Ostcombe

Pelde Stenson is the daughter of Matho and Ismira Stenson. She married Davus Stenworth at Torton and the couple lived there from then on. Their daughter Dalis was born later, and the family still lived in Torton. No later passage says Pelde Stenson moved away. A chapter 32 passage places her in Torton as well.

Answer: Torton

Nylia Corrford died in Chapter 5. Jotho Thornmere's first move away from Ostcombe is in Chapter 39, when he took lodgings in Quenford. He was born into a family living in Ostcombe, and in Chapter 16 he married and the couple lived in Ostcombe from then on. Nothing before Chapter 5 shows him moving elsewhere, so he was in Ostcombe when she died.

Answer: Ostcombe

Malis Prydenridge's death is recorded in Chapter 7. At that point Peten Haskick still lived in Dunstead, where the household was placed in Chapter 1. He did not move to Staveford until Chapter 14, and later to Quenford and Gulhaven.

Answer: Dunstead

Islan Thornmere died in Chapter 29 (¶4979), at Dungate. In the same chapter (¶4995), Gadrek Prydenridge married in the chapel at Ostcombe, and the couple lived in Ostcombe from then on. Nothing later shows Gadrek moving elsewhere.

Whether the wedding comes before or after Islan's death within Chapter 29 is not clear from the paragraph numbers alone. The marriage paragraph (¶4995) comes after the death paragraph (¶4979), so Gadrek was presumably living in Ostcombe at the time of the death either way. Before the marriage he also lived in Ostcombe, since his household was there and he was in Ostcombe in earlier chapters.

Answer: Ostcombe

Pelde Stenson married Davus Stenworth in Torton (Chapter 8), and the couple lived in Torton from then on. Their daughter Dalis was born in Torton in Chapter 15. Later mentions, such as Chapter 32's "In Torton. Pelde Stenson told Pelde Stenworth...", are also set in Torton. No record of a move appears.

Ulrald Corrford died in Chapter 21, so the latest relevant information places Pelde Stenson in Torton.

Answer: Torton

Pewyn Stenenridge's death is recorded in Chapter 19. At that point, Taric Corrley's latest move was in Chapter 16, when he quit Kelmere and took lodgings in Staveford. He did not leave Staveford for Dungate until Chapter 23, after Pewyn's death.

Answer: Staveford

Nelan died in Chapter 16 (¶3169). At that time, Rorald Lindmere was in the river crossing at Kelmere (Chapter 16 ¶3245 places him there). He moved to Salcombe only in Chapter 19.

Answer: Kelmere

Orrald Stenson, also called "Orrald the Younger", died of a festering wound at Torton in Chapter 8. At that point Havie Prydenridge was still living with her family in Ostcombe. She did not move away (to Staveford) until Chapter 36.

Answer: Ostcombe

Pelde Stenworth married Sebin Brackick at Torton in Chapter 34 and the couple lived in Torton from then on. In Chapter 37 she gave birth to a daughter and the family lived in Torton. Marald Corrford's death at Ravenmere comes in Chapter 39. No later record shows her moving away.

Answer: Torton

Ismira died in Chapter 37 (buried at Kelmere). Kassa Stenson's moves: Chapter 34 ¶5681 "Kassa Stenson went along to live in Kelmere as well." That is the latest move before Chapter 37. Ismira moved to Kelmere in Chapter 33, and Kassa followed in Chapter 34. No later move for Kassa appears.

Answer: Kelmere

Gazek Stenson died in Chapter 5. At that time, the Stenenridge household lived in the harbor town of Dunstead (Chapter 1). Thizek was living at home with his parents. No move for Thizek appears before Chapter 5. (Rozek's move to Wilwick is in Chapter 13, and Thizek's later move to Elmhaven is in Chapter 38.)

Answer: Dunstead

Havus Stenworth moved from Torton to Gulhaven in Chapter 7. Ludrek Prydenridge died in Chapter 11. The next recorded move for Havus is to Yarlby in Chapter 34, so he was still in Gulhaven when Ludrek died.

Answer: Gulhaven

Harine Lindmere married Orrald Stenson (Chapter 1, ¶278). Nothing later in the record says he died or that they separated. The only death claim in the excerpts is a rumor about Ismira Stenson, and a rumor is not a fact. Harine later moved to Wilwick, but "went along to live" suggests only a move.

Answer: Orrald Stenson

Zalis Corrley's husband died of a long wasting sickness at Kelmere (Chapter 18). Later, in Chapter 26, Ferald and Zalis Corrley were wed at Dunstead. Nothing after that suggests Ferald died or that they separated, so Ferald is the latest spouse. His full name is not given beyond "Ferald."

Answer: Ferald

Pelde Stenworth, daughter of Havus Stenworth, started out married to Gazek Stenson (Chapter 1). In Chapter 34 she married Sebin Brackick at Torton, and in Chapter 37 she bore him a daughter, Elvie Brackick. Nothing later changes this. The Pelde Stenson who married Davus Stenworth in Chapter 8 is a different woman.

Answer: Sebin Brackick

Matho Stenson's daughter Pelde Stenson married Davus Stenworth at Torton in Chapter 8. They had a daughter, Dalis, in Chapter 15. Nothing in the record says Davus died, and he is still speaking in Chapter 38.

The Pelde Stenworth who marries Sebin Brackick in Chapter 34 is a different person. She is Havus Stenworth's daughter and Gazek Stenson's widow, since Gazek died in Chapter 5.

Answer: Davus Stenworth

Lura Haskick's husband is Peten Haskick. The latest entries show him moving to Gulhaven (Chapter 39) with Lura going along. No entry records his death or any other spouse for her.

Answer: Peten Haskick

Yewyn Corrford married Kadan Corrley at Kelmere in Chapter 16. Kadan Corrley still appears in Chapter 19, and nothing later records his death or a separation. The other Yewyns (Haskick) are different people.

Answer: Kadan Corrley

Havus Stenworth's wife is Fewyn Stenworth (Chapter 1). Rumor in Chapter 4 that Tatho Brackick secretly married Fewyn is gossip, not fact. Havus moved to Gulhaven and Fewyn followed him. Later Fewyn moved to Yarlby and Havus went along. In the last chapter Havus rode to Torton, but nothing says the marriage ended or that Fewyn died.

Answer: Fewyn Stenworth

Kadan Corrley married Yewyn Corrford at Kelmere (Chapter 16). Later chapters, such as Chapter 19, still show Yewyn Corrford as his wife. Nothing in the record reports a death or another marriage for either of them.

Answer: Yewyn Corrford

Movie Prydenridge married the only son of Luena Stenenridge in Chapter 28. Chapter 38 says a daughter, Kamira Stenenridge, was born to Movie Prydenridge and Thizek Stenenridge. So the husband is Thizek Stenenridge. Nothing in the record says he died.

Answer: Thizek Stenenridge

Isric Thornmere married Havie (Prydenridge) at Ostcombe in Chapter 28. No later paragraph mentions a death or a separation. In Chapter 39, "Isric Thornmere went along to live in Dunby as well" does not say he left her. Chapter 40 still has Havie Prydenridge in scenes with Isric, giving him a promise and talking with him.

Answer: Havie Prydenridge

Ferald Stenworth wed Zalis Corrley at Dunstead in Chapter 26 and the couple lived there from then on. Nothing later in the record mentions Zalis dying or the marriage ending.

Answer: Zalis Corrley

Yera Haskick is the eldest daughter of Peten and Lura Haskick. In Chapter 29, Gadrek Prydenridge married Lura Haskick's eldest daughter in the chapel at Ostcombe. The earlier claim in Chapter 27 that Islan Thornmere had secretly married her is only a whisper, so it doesn't count as fact. Gadrek is still alive in Chapter 31, and nothing later ends the marriage.

Answer: Gadrek Prydenridge

Movus Brackick married Dalis Stenworth in the chapel at Yarlby (Chapter 39), and they lived in Yarlby from then on. In Chapter 40 Dalis gave birth to their son, Iszek Brackick. Nothing in the record says Dalis died or that the marriage ended.

Answer: Dalis Stenworth

Luena Stenenridge is the wife of Rozek Stenenridge. Nothing in the record says either of them died or that they separated. Chapter 31 has Luena settling in Ostcombe and Rozek following to live there as well. Rozek appears again in later chapters (33, 36, 37), so he is still alive and still with her.

Answer: Rozek Stenenridge

Bremira Corrford married Zavus Prydenridge in Chapter 25. A later mention in Chapter 31 says she told people Rovus Prydenridge had drowned, but that is a different person and does not say anything about Zavus's death. Chapter 26 shows Zavus alive. No record of his death or of a separation appears.

Answer: Zavus Prydenridge

The record states in Chapter 18 that Yedan Corrford died of a kick from a cart horse at Dunstead. The later mentions of Yedan (a letter-related note in Chapter 21 involves only the youngest son and Fenelle, not Yedan acting) do not contradict this death.

Answer: no

Orrald Stenson is also called "Orrald the Younger" (Chapter 1, ¶649). The record says in Chapter 8 ¶2174 that "Orrald the Younger died of a wound that festered at Torton." Later chapters give nothing that contradicts this.

Answer: no

Chapter 5 records that Gazek Stenson died of a wound that festered at Torton. The later excerpts contain nothing that contradicts this or says he returned to life, so he is not alive at the end of the record.

Answer: no

Chapter 29 records that Islan Thornmere died of old age, quietly in his sleep at Dungate. Later mentions of him do not contradict this. The Chapter 12 claim that he drowned was a rumor, and the Chapter 27 marriage gossip is also unconfirmed. Either way, the latest firm information is his death.

Answer: no

Gadan Corrley was married to Zalis Corrley. In Chapter 18 the record says "The husband of Zalis Corrley died of a long wasting sickness at Kelmere." Gadan's last appearances as a living person are in Chapters 12 and 16, before that death. Later mentions, such as "the youngest son of Gadan Corrley" in Chapter 22, only identify him as a parent and don't show him alive.

Answer: no

In Chapter 37, the record says a festering wound took Ismira Stenson that summer and that she was buried at Kelmere. The earlier rumor of her death from plague (Chapter 8) was only gossip. This later death is stated as fact, and nothing after it says otherwise.

Answer: no

In Chapter 16, "That spring, the coughing sickness took Nelan; he was buried at Kelford." This is a death. Later mentions in Chapter 34 and 36 refer to "the youngest son of Nelan Brackick" and "the youngest son of Volia Brackick", which are references to a parent's child and do not imply Nelan is still alive. No later information contradicts the death.

Answer: no

In Chapter 21, Ulrald Corrford was buried in the churchyard at Staveford, having died of old age. His belongings, the silver flute and the amber map, went to Kassa Brackick. Later mentions of "Ulrald" appear only in chapters before his death, and no later passage shows him alive.

Answer: no

Chapter 7 records that Malis Prydenridge was laid in the churchyard at Ostcombe, dead of a long wasting sickness. Nothing later in the record says otherwise. The only later mention is a letter that calls the youngest son "of Malis Prydenridge", which only identifies him by his mother.

Answer: no

The latest relevant information is in Chapter 39, which says Marald Corrford was laid in the churchyard at Ravenmere, dead of a fall from the mill loft. So he is not alive at the end of the record.

Answer: no

In Chapter 5, a long wasting sickness took Nylia Corrford and she was buried at Dunstead. Later mentions in Chapter 23 name Bremira and Elra Corrford, not Nylia, and nothing indicates she is alive afterward.

Answer: no

In Chapter 22, Volia Brackick was laid in the churchyard at Kelford, dead of drowning in the flood. Chapters 34 and later mention only her youngest son, and nothing there says she is alive again.

Answer: no

Wenelle Lindmere appears in the record through Chapter 37, where she is still active, and she has a child born in Kelmere. The claim that she drowned (Chapter 10) is a rumor by Ismira Stenson, and she is shown alive afterwards. No later passage says she died.

Answer: yes

Matho Stenson was alive in the latest events: a rumor of his death by plague (Chapters 18 and 24) is just a rumor. Later, in Chapter 39, he sends a parcel to Luvie Prydenridge. He also fell asleep in a chair in the same chapter, and nothing records his death.

Answer: yes

The only claim of death is a rumor in Chapter 21, started by the second daughter of Rorald Lindmere and traced to a peddler. A rumor is not a fact. Later chapters show Pelde Stenworth alive and active: she married Sebin Brackick in Chapter 34, gave birth to Elvie Brackick in Chapter 37, and appears in ordinary scenes in Chapter 38.

Answer: yes

The only claims that Matho Stenson died are rumors (Chapter 18 and Chapter 24, both attributed to a peddler), and rumors are not facts. Later records show him active: he moved to Staveford, went to live in Kelmere, laughed at a story in Chapter 37, fell asleep in a chair in Chapter 39, and in Chapter 39 sent a parcel to Luvie Prydenridge. Nothing in the record says he died.

Answer: yes

The only mention of Rorald's death is a rumor (Chapter 30, started by Movie Prydenridge from a peddler), which is not a fact. He appears active in later chapters (32, 36, 40), so he is still alive at the end.

Answer: yes

Chapter 31 has only a rumor that Rovus Prydenridge drowned, and no body was ever seen. In later chapters he is still active: he complains of his back in Chapter 32, talks about the price of salt in Chapter 35, and in Chapter 37 he has a son, Madan, with Wenelle Lindmere. The rumor is not a fact, and the latest evidence shows him alive.

Answer: yes

No death of Ilrald Prydenridge is recorded. The latest information about him is in Chapter 38, where he left Torton and settled in Wilwick. The only death-related items concern others: a rumor about Rorald Lindmere, and Bremira's claim about Rovus Prydenridge, who is not Ilrald.

Answer: yes

The material records no death for Yewyn Corrford. The latest mentions, in Chapter 37, show her active: scrubbing the step and talking with Febin Prydenridge. The Chapter 32 line about following someone to Wilholt concerns Yewyn Haskick, a different person.

Answer: yes

There is no record of Kassa Stenson dying. The latest mention (Chapter 37) shows her sorting old letters, and she moved to Kelmere in Chapter 34, still living.

Answer: yes

Bremira Corrford is last mentioned in Chapter 39 (¶6294), where she receives a parcel from Lura Haskick containing the silver chalice. No death is recorded for her anywhere in the excerpts. The drowning in Chapter 31 concerns Rovus Prydenridge, not her.

Answer: yes

Istho Stenworth appears throughout the record up to Chapter 39 (the last mention is in Chapter 39 ¶6264, where Istho is still talking), and nothing in the material says Istho died.

Answer: yes

Kassa Brackick appears throughout the record, with her latest mentions in Chapter 40 (arguing with the carter, telling Jotho Thornmere a secret). There is no mention of her death anywhere in the material, so she is still alive at the end.

Answer: yes

Taric Corrley appears in the record up to Chapter 34, where he moves from Dungate to Kelmere. No passage reports his death. The only death in the material is the death of Zalis Corrley's husband (Chapter 18), and that is Gadan Corrley, not Taric.

Answer: yes

The silver flute first belonged to Ulrald Corrford (Chapter 1). In Chapter 21 it went to Kassa Brackick. Nothing later in the record moves it again, so Kassa Brackick holds it at the end.

Answer: Kassa Brackick

The jade mirror starts with Rozek Stenenridge (Ch. 1). He gives it to Luena Stenenridge (Ch. 5), and it passes back and forth between them in Ch. 16 and Ch. 23. In the last relevant passage (Ch. 36), Rozek presses it into the hands of Luvie Prydenridge and takes nothing for it.

Answer: Luvie Prydenridge

Tracing the oak lantern:
- Ch 1: Luena Stenenridge kept it.
- Ch 12: Luena gave it to Rozek Stenenridge.
- Ch 18: Rozek sent it by carrier to Rovus Prydenridge, who received it.
- Ch 19: Wenelle Lindmere won it from Rovus at cards, and kept it.

No later transfer appears. The Ch 21 "Fenelle Lindmere" entry is only about staying in place and has nothing to do with the lantern.

Answer: Wenelle Lindmere

The latest event in the record for the copper chalice is in Chapter 35, where Isric Thornmere won it from Gadrek Prydenridge at cards, fairly, and kept it. Earlier, Luena Stenenridge sent it to Yera Stenworth (Chapter 29), and Gadrek then won it from Yera (Chapter 31).

Answer: Isric Thornmere

Tracing the oak comb: Isric Thornmere possessed it (Ch 1), and in Chapter 22 Isric sent the oak comb by carrier to Kassa Brackick, who received it safely. No later transfer is recorded.

Answer: Kassa Brackick

The pewter dagger passed through several hands:

- It began with Yewyn Haskick (Ch 1).
- Yewyn gave it to the youngest son of Volia Brackick (Ch 19).
- A parcel from the youngest son of Nelan Brackick sent it to Jotho Thornmere (Ch 20). Volia and Nelan may be a naming inconsistency, but the "youngest son of ... Brackick" link makes this the likely next step.
- Yera Stenworth won it from "Quiet Jotho" at cards, fairly, and kept it (Ch 40). I take Quiet Jotho to be Jotho Thornmere.

The latest information shows Yera Stenworth keeping the dagger.

Answer: Yera Stenworth

Brass map: belonged to Ismira Stenson (Ch 1), and in Ch 14 Ismira Stenson gave it to Matho Stenson. No later transfer of the brass map appears in the material.

Answer: Matho Stenson

Tracing the amber map: it belonged to Tatho Brackick, then a parcel from Tatho reached Marald (Ch. 11), who kept it. Later, the youngest son of Yedan Corrford gave it to Ulrald Corrford (Ch. 14). Then it went to Kassa Brackick (Ch. 21), who gave it to Volan Stenworth (Ch. 30). Finally, Volan Stenworth pressed it into the hands of Rimor Corrford (Ch. 33).

The latest information shows Rimor Corrford holding it.

Answer: Rimor Corrford

Tracing the silver chalice: Kassa Brackick owned it (Ch 1), pressed it into the hands of Quiet Peten (Ch 5). Peten Haskick pressed it into the hands of Lura Haskick (Ch 19). In Ch 39, a parcel from Lura Haskick reached Bremira Corrford, and the silver chalice was now hers to keep.

Answer: Bremira Corrford

The ivory lantern belonged to Ismira Stenson (Ch. 1). In Chapter 32, Ismira Stenson pressed it into the hands of Rimor Corrford, giving it away freely. No later passage records it moving again.

Answer: Rimor Corrford

Tracing the bone compass chain:
- Ulrald Corrford → Fenelle Lindmere (Ch 17)
- Fenelle → only son of Luena Stenenridge (Ch 18)
- Thizek Stenenridge sent it to Lura (Ch 21), who received it
- Lura Haskick sent it to Volan Stenworth (Ch 24)
- Wife of Volan Stenworth won it from Volan at cards (Ch 27)
- Kassa Brackick gave it to Ismira (Ch 31)
- Ismira Stenson owned it, and it went to Matho Stenson (Ch 37)
- Matho Stenson's parcel reached Luvie Prydenridge, who keeps it (Ch 39)

The latest holder is Luvie Prydenridge.

Answer: Luvie Prydenridge

The only ownership information for the ivory chalice is that it belonged to Ludrek Prydenridge, head of the Prydenridge household. The custom that it passes to the eldest living child applies only on the holder's death, and the excerpts record no such death or any other transfer of it.

Answer: Ludrek Prydenridge

Silver flute history: it belonged to Ulrald Corrford (Ch. 1), then went to Kassa Brackick (Ch. 21). No later transfer is mentioned, so the current holder is Kassa Brackick, and the holder immediately before was Ulrald Corrford.

Answer: Ulrald Corrford

The jade mirror started with Rozek Stenenridge and passed back and forth between him and Luena Stenenridge. In the latest transfer (Chapter 36), Rozek gave it to Luvie Prydenridge, so Luvie is the current holder and Rozek held it immediately before.

Answer: Rozek Stenenridge

The oak lantern passed from Luena Stenenridge to Rozek Stenenridge (Ch. 12), then to Rovus Prydenridge (Ch. 18). Wenelle Lindmere then won it from Rovus at cards and kept it (Ch. 19), so Wenelle is the current holder and Rovus held it immediately before.

Answer: Rovus Prydenridge

The copper chalice passed from Luena Stenenridge to Yera Stenworth (sent by carrier), then to Gadrek, who won it from Yera at cards. In the latest event, Isric Thornmere won it from Gadrek Prydenridge at cards. So the current holder is Isric Thornmere, and the holder immediately before was Gadrek Prydenridge.

Answer: Gadrek Prydenridge

The oak comb was among Isric Thornmere's possessions (Chapter 1). In Chapter 22 Isric sent it by carrier to Kassa Brackick, who received it. Kassa Brackick is therefore the current holder, and Isric Thornmere held it immediately before.

Answer: Isric Thornmere

The latest event is in Chapter 40: Yera Stenworth won the pewter dagger from "Quiet Jotho" at cards and kept it. Quiet Jotho is presumably Jotho Thornmere, who received the dagger in Chapter 20. So Jotho Thornmere held it immediately before Yera Stenworth.

Answer: Jotho Thornmere

Brass map: belonged to Ismira Stenson (Ch 1), then Ismira gave it to Matho Stenson (Ch 14). The current holder is Matho Stenson, and the one immediately before was Ismira Stenson.

Answer: Ismira Stenson

The amber map's chain of holders, in order:

- Tatho Brackick owned it, then sent it to Marald (Ch 11).
- The youngest son of Yedan Corrford gave it to Ulrald Corrford (Ch 14).
- Ulrald Corrford's map went to Kassa Brackick (Ch 21).
- Kassa Brackick gave it to Volan Stenworth (Ch 30).
- Volan Stenworth pressed it into the hands of Rimor Corrford (Ch 33), the latest transfer, so Rimor Corrford is the current holder.

The holder immediately before Rimor Corrford was Volan Stenworth.

Answer: Volan Stenworth

Tracing the silver chalice chronologically:

- Ch 1: Kassa Brackick possessed it.
- Ch 5: Kassa Brackick gave it to Quiet Peten (Peten Haskick).
- Ch 19: Peten Haskick pressed it into the hands of Lura Haskick.
- Ch 39: A parcel from Lura Haskick reached Bremira Corrford; the chalice is now hers to keep.

The current holder is Bremira Corrford, and the one before her was Lura Haskick.

Answer: Lura Haskick

The ivory lantern first belonged to Ismira Stenson. In Chapter 32 she gave it to Rimor Corrford. No later passage moves it again, so Rimor Corrford is the current holder and Ismira Stenson held it immediately before.

Answer: Ismira Stenson

The bone compass passed down a chain of holders. Ismira Stenson owned it and it went to Matho Stenson. Matho Stenson then sent it in a parcel to Luvie Prydenridge, who keeps it. Luvie Prydenridge is the current holder, so the one before was Matho Stenson.

Answer: Matho Stenson

Movie Prydenridge's father is Rovus Prydenridge (Chapter 6). Rovus's father is Ludrek Prydenridge, head of the household with children including Rovus (Chapter 1).

Answer: Ludrek Prydenridge

Rimor Corrford's parents are Kassa Brackick (mother) and Ulrald Corrford (father). The question is about the maternal grandmother, so we need Kassa Brackick's mother. The material does not name Kassa's parents anywhere.

Answer: unknown

Madan Prydenridge's father is Rovus Prydenridge (mother Wenelle Lindmere). Rovus's parents are Ludrek Prydenridge and Malis Prydenridge. So the paternal grandmother is Malis Prydenridge.

Answer: Malis Prydenridge

Nerine's father is Rovus Prydenridge, whose parents are Ludrek Prydenridge and Malis Prydenridge. The paternal grandmother is therefore Malis, Ludrek's wife.

Answer: Malis Prydenridge

The record names Iszek Brackick's mother as Dalis Stenworth, but none of the excerpts say who her parents are. Pelde Stenworth, Lurald Stenworth and Volan Stenworth appear, but nothing links any of them to Dalis as her mother. Iszek's maternal grandmother therefore can't be determined from this material.

Answer: unknown

Istho Stenworth's father is Lurald Stenworth (Chapter 25: a son born to Nerine Prydenridge and Lurald Stenworth). Lurald's parents are Havus Stenworth and Fewyn Stenworth (Chapter 1 household). So the paternal grandmother is Fewyn Stenworth.

Answer: Fewyn Stenworth

Febin Prydenridge's father is Rovus Prydenridge, whose parents are Ludrek Prydenridge and Malis Prydenridge. Rovus's mother is Malis, so Febin's paternal grandmother is Malis Prydenridge.

Answer: Malis Prydenridge

Ferald Stenworth is the son of Luwyn Brackick and Lurald Stenworth (Chapter 10). Lurald Stenworth is the son of Havus Stenworth and Fewyn Stenworth (Chapter 1). Ferald's paternal grandfather is therefore Havus Stenworth.

Answer: Havus Stenworth

Elra Corrford is the daughter of Fenelle Lindmere and Marald Corrford. Her maternal grandfather is therefore Fenelle Lindmere's father. The material doesn't name Fenelle Lindmere's parents, so this isn't given. (Her paternal grandfather is Yedan Corrford, but the question asks about the maternal side.)

Answer: unknown

Bremira Corrford is the daughter of Ulrald Corrford and Kassa Brackick. Ulrald is the eldest son of Yedan Corrford and Nylia Corrford. This makes Yedan Corrford her paternal grandfather.

Answer: Yedan Corrford

Kamira Stenenridge is the daughter of Thizek Stenenridge (Chapter 38). Thizek's parents are Rozek Stenenridge and Luena Stenenridge (Chapter 1). Thizek is Rozek's son, so Rozek is Kamira's paternal grandfather.

Answer: Rozek Stenenridge

Semor Brackick's parents are Yewyn Haskick and Tatho Brackick. His maternal grandfather is therefore Yewyn Haskick's father, and the material never names him.

Answer: unknown

Movus Brackick is the son of Rinelle Corrley and Kadrek Brackick (Chapter 25). His maternal grandmother is therefore Rinelle Corrley's mother.

The excerpts name Rinelle Corrley but never say who her parents are. The Corrley family isn't described anywhere in the material.

Answer: unknown

Zavus Prydenridge's mother is Wenelle (Lindmere), and his father is Rovus Prydenridge. His maternal grandfather would be Wenelle Lindmere's father. The material mentions Rorald Lindmere only in a rumor that he was dead of plague, and it never states that he is Wenelle's father. No parent of Wenelle is named.

Answer: unknown
